dependencies.reason: uses its workspace record, its access decision and its lock, which a merge job waits on rather than being refused by
merges inside the repository its store holds
rebases and detects conflicts through its history engine, which also guarantees the result matches the real git binary

tasks.title: Run a merge job and record its outcome
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the merge job integration test file, and confirm they fail
Define the merge job record with its statuses and documented fields, and a migration the second target runs too
Run the job through the platform's queue, waiting its turn for the workspace lock rather than refusing a busy workspace
Rebase the source onto the target through the history engine and fast-forward the target to the result, producing no merge commit
Record the target's head before as base_sha and after as merged_sha, and leave both null until the job completes
End a conflicting job as failed with the conflicting files recorded and the target branch at the head it had before

tasks.title: Submit merge jobs and refuse the ones that cannot run
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the merge routes' test files, and confirm they fail
Validate the body before the workspace is looked up: both names required, both following git's branch-name rules
Confirm the workspace is ready and both branches exist, refusing with 400 otherwise
Queue the job and answer 202 with it at status queued, carrying the submitting user
Refuse a merge of the same source into the same target that is already queued or running with 409 duplicate_merge, leaving the existing job alone

tasks.title: List, read, cancel and requeue merge jobs
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the merge routes' test files, and confirm they fail
List a workspace's jobs capped at 200 and read one, answering 404 for an unknown id and for a job of another workspace alike
Cancel a queued job so it never runs and the target is untouched, refusing any other status with 409
Requeue a dead-lettered job to queued, refusing any other status with 409 and refusing one whose source and target are already queued or running

tasks.title: Rebase several branches in one request
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the batch rebase test files, and confirm they fail
Validate the body before the workspace: a target ref, a non-empty list of at most 20 branches, each following git's branch-name rules, naming an offending branch by its index
Take the workspace lock without waiting, answering 409 workspace_busy when it is held
Rebase each branch onto the target in turn through the history engine while the request waits, continuing past a branch that conflicts or errors
Answer with one result per branch in the order given: ok with the new head, conflict with the conflicting files, or error
Leave every branch either at its new head or at the head it had before, including when the rebase itself fails with 500

tasks.title: Make a job survive a restart and a stall
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the merge job integration test file, and confirm they fail
Make a job that was running when its component restarted come back as queued, completed or failed, never as running with nothing running it
Dead-letter a job that has made no progress for 15 minutes, recording its retry count, and let a requeue return it to the queue
Make the fast-forward of the target atomic with respect to the job, so the target holds either its previous head or the merged result and never an intermediate commit

tasks.title: Verify merging and batch rebasing against a running deployment
steps: Add the three smoke tests and confirm each passes against a running deployment with the real afc binary, or skips with a message naming what was missing
Trace 10-PATH-1: the submit validates and queues, the job waits for package 03's real lock, the history engine of package 06 rebases against package 05's store, and the target is fast-forwarded
Trace 10-PATH-2: the conflict comes from the real engine and the job's conflict_files carries the engine's path list unchanged
Trace 10-PATH-3: the batch rebase drives the same engine synchronously and reports a result per branch

For every criterion carrying a contract, confirm a caller in production code consumes the producer's result and not only a test: the history engine is called by both the job and the batch rebase, the lock by both, and the job record by the list, read, cancel and requeue routes
Confirm a merge job queues rather than being refused while another operation holds the lock, which distinguishes it from the sync and the archive
Grep src/merge/ and the files every task's touches lists for TODO, FIXME and the project's not-implemented marker, and remove any that remain
Add the merge conformance cases to the harness from package 01
done_when: `make check` passes with no network access and no deployment configured
afc merge submit, list, status, cancel and requeue and afc rebase submit behave as docs/prd/cli.md specifies against a running deployment
